newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will be given a red carpet reception when he arrives in Dhaka on Saturday on a two-day official visit to Bangladesh.
Some 157,000 cyclone affected people will given free food for two months.
President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed on Friday urged the political parties not to engage students as their partners in politcs and power games.
Opposition leader and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia on Friday alleged the government's relief activities were plagued by ineptness and planning weaknesses.
Nancy Powell, Charge D Affaires of the U.S. embassy in Dhaka, on Friday announced the U.S. government would provide $25,000 as emeregency relief for cyclone affected people in Bangladesh.
A plan is underway to set up government primary school in each village as part of the government's drive to eradicate illiteracy by the next ten years.

The Power Development Board (PDB) on Thursday singed an agreement with Enron Internationl and Associates to set up a 100 megawatt barge-mounted power plant, opening door to the first investment by a foreign power development company.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved Friday a $100 million loan to fund a primary education project in Bangladesh that is to benefit about six million students. REUTER
